title: KnowTrace: Bootstrapping Iterative Retrieval-Augmented Generation with Structured Knowledge Tracing

problem.claim: Iterative retrieval-augmented generation for complex multi-hop questions can overload the language model as context grows and critical information becomes harder to connect.

gap.claim: Existing methods typically accumulate retrieved contents through alternating reasoning and retrieval without explicitly organizing the information to mitigate context overload or support higher-quality multi-step reasoning.

contributions.claim: KnowTrace autonomously traces desired knowledge triplets and organizes them into a question-relevant knowledge graph.
KnowTrace uses knowledge backtracing to identify contributive language-model generations as process-supervision data for self-bootstrapping.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that KnowTrace consistently surpasses existing methods across three multi-hop question-answering benchmarks.
The authors report that the bootstrapped version further amplifies the gains.

narrative_sequence.summary: Iterative retrieval-augmented generation supports complex multi-hop question answering.
Alternating reasoning and retrieval can create growing context overload and make connections among important information harder to perceive.
KnowTrace organizes desired knowledge triplets into a relevant knowledge graph and uses backtracing for process supervision and self-bootstrapping.
The authors report gains over existing methods on three multi-hop question-answering benchmarks, with further gains from bootstrapping.

source_observation.claim: The framework replaces simple accumulation of retrieved contents with structured knowledge-triplet organization and reflective backtracing.

interpretation.claim: Explicit structure and process-level feedback may help multi-step reasoning systems manage retrieved information and improve subsequent reasoning.

application.claim: For iterative retrieval systems, consider structured intermediate representations together with feedback from contributive reasoning steps.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify when structured tracing or backtracing may be ineffective.

unknowns: The three benchmark names, evaluation metrics, baselines, and quantitative results are not specified.
The abstract does not detail the knowledge-tracing algorithm, bootstrapping procedure, or experimental conditions.
